claims.source_name: Office of the Governor of West Virginia
claims.text: The Office of the Governor of West Virginia's own announcement states that on 21 July 2026, following severe storms producing flash flooding, landslides, road closures, damaging winds, torrential rainfall and mudslides across the state, Governor Patrick Morrisey declared a State of Emergency for all 55 West Virginia counties, effective for 30 days unless terminated earlier, with the most severe impacts concentrated in Lewis, Pleasants and Upshur counties.

claims.source_name: Office of the Governor of West Virginia
claims.text: The governor's office's 22 July 2026 flood-response update states that 'approximately 85 rescues have been carried out over the last 20 hours,' with more than 3,100 Division of Highways employees and over 300 pieces of heavy equipment deployed, roughly 12,366 customers without power statewide, and three emergency shelters open (Buckhannon, Weston, Philippi).

claims.source_name: Office of the Governor of West Virginia
claims.text: The governor's office's 24 July 2026 flood recovery update reports approximately 151 homes damaged in Upshur County, a National Guard deployment of 352 personnel and 84 vehicles, debris removal of 84 tons in Upshur County and 192 tons in Lewis County in a 24-hour period, more than 2,600 Division of Highways employees and 1,000 pieces of equipment, 134 Department of Environmental Protection staff using 130 vehicles, more than 500 site inspections completed, and over 1,700 registered volunteers.

claims.source_name: Office of the Governor of West Virginia
claims.text: The governor's office's 14 August 2026 announcement states the State of Emergency is extended through 19 September 2026 for Barbour, Doddridge, Harrison, Lewis, Pendleton, Pleasants, Randolph, Ritchie, Tucker, Tyler, Upshur and Wetzel counties so that recovery operations and damage assessments can continue, while the State of Emergency for the remaining 43 counties expires 20 August 2026; Governor Morrisey is quoted: 'West Virginians have made tremendous progress cleaning up and recovering from these storms, but there is still a lot of work ahead in some of our hardest-hit communities.'

description: Severe storms brought torrential rainfall to north-central West Virginia on 20-21 July 2026, triggering flash flooding, landslides, mudslides, damaging winds and road closures. Governor Patrick Morrisey declared a State of Emergency for all 55 West Virginia counties on 21 July 2026, with the most severe impacts concentrated in Lewis, Pleasants and Upshur counties. The governor's office reported approximately 85 rescues over a 20-hour span on 22 July, more than 3,100 Division of Highways employees and over 300 pieces of heavy equipment deployed, roughly 12,366 customers without power and three shelters open at Buckhannon, Weston and Philippi; by 24 July it recorded about 151 homes damaged in Upshur County and a National Guard deployment of 352 personnel and 84 vehicles, alongside over 1,700 registered volunteers. On 14 August 2026 the state extended the emergency through 19 September 2026 for twelve hard-hit counties -- Barbour, Doddridge, Harrison, Lewis, Pendleton, Pleasants, Randolph, Ritchie, Tucker, Tyler, Upshur and Wetzel -- so recovery operations and damage assessments can continue, while the declaration for the remaining 43 counties expires 20 August 2026.

impact.summary: The West Virginia governor's office reported approximately 85 water rescues over a 20-hour span on 22 July 2026, about 151 homes damaged in Upshur County, and a National Guard deployment that had grown to 352 personnel and 84 vehicles by 24 July, alongside more than 2,600 Division of Highways employees and over 1,700 registered volunteers. A State of Emergency covering all 55 counties was declared 21 July 2026 and later extended through 19 September 2026 for twelve of the hardest-hit counties, while the declaration for the remaining 43 counties expires 20 August 2026. No death or displacement figure has been confirmed by an authoritative source, though media reporting attributes two deaths in Upshur County to the flooding.

updates.text: The State of Emergency was extended through 19 September 2026 for twelve counties -- Barbour, Doddridge, Harrison, Lewis, Pendleton, Pleasants, Randolph, Ritchie, Tucker, Tyler, Upshur and Wetzel -- to let recovery operations and damage assessments continue; it expires 20 August 2026 in the remaining 43 counties.

The governor's office's recovery update recorded about 151 homes damaged in Upshur County, a National Guard deployment of 352 personnel and 84 vehicles, debris removal of 84 tons in Upshur and 192 tons in Lewis County in a 24-hour period, more than 2,600 Division of Highways employees and over 1,700 registered volunteers.

Approximately 85 rescues were carried out over 20 hours, with more than 3,100 Division of Highways employees and over 300 pieces of heavy equipment deployed, roughly 12,366 customers without power statewide and three emergency shelters open at Buckhannon, Weston and Philippi.

Governor Patrick Morrisey declared a State of Emergency for all 55 West Virginia counties, effective for 30 days unless terminated earlier, after storms brought flash flooding, landslides, mudslides and damaging winds; impacts were most severe in Lewis, Pleasants and Upshur counties.
